policy.statement: Every applicable EF Core relational specification behavior must run. A skip is permitted only for a primary-source-backed database-engine limitation, an upstream EF Core limitation reached before provider-owned translation can solve it, or a structurally inapplicable historical test.
engineLimitationRequirements: At least one official database-vendor primary source
A retrieval date for every source
A reproducible probe against every affected supported target
frameworkLimitationRequirements: The upstream EF Core specification test is itself skipped and is backed by either its linked dotnet/efcore issue or both the exact upstream skip source and the framework enforcement source
The failure is reproduced with the upstream skip disabled
The failure is attributable to framework-owned translation or semantics rather than provider SQL capability
A retrieval date and concrete re-evaluation trigger

activeDispositions.summary: MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.4 immediately enforce a self-referencing NO ACTION foreign key while deleting a set that contains both the dependent and principal rows.

primarySources.title: FOREIGN KEY Constraints
primarySources.supports: The Referential Actions section states that InnoDB treats NO ACTION as RESTRICT and immediately rejects a parent delete while a related foreign-key value exists. The same page explicitly permits self-referential foreign keys.

primarySources.title: Foreign Keys
primarySources.supports: The Constraints section states that RESTRICT is the default ON DELETE behavior, NO ACTION is its synonym, and the change fails with error 1451 when a child row exists.

observations.result: Both sync and async invocations fail with error 1451 because Animals.EagleId still references the selected principal row when InnoDB checks the delete.
Both sync and async invocations fail with the same error 1451 and self-referencing Animals.EagleId constraint.

activeDispositions.providerWorkaroundAssessment: The provider already isolates the target-table subquery, so the statement reaches execution. Nulling or deleting dependent rows first would require extra DML, would change the configured NO ACTION relationship semantics when a dependent is outside the query result, and would change ExecuteDelete's affected-row contract. Disabling foreign_key_checks would weaken integrity for the whole session. No general single-statement rewrite can preserve the query, relationship, and row-count semantics under immediate RESTRICT enforcement.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when MySQL or MariaDB documents statement-end NO ACTION checks for InnoDB, or when a supported target replaces MariaDB 11.4. MariaDB 11.8 remains active because this exact specification case passes there.

activeDispositions.summary: MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.4/11.8 do not provide a predicate clause for partial or filtered indexes.

primarySources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: CREATE INDEX Statement
primarySources.supports: The complete CREATE INDEX grammar permits column, prefix, or functional key parts followed by index, algorithm, and lock options; it defines no WHERE predicate or partial-index clause.

primarySources.title: CREATE INDEX
primarySources.supports: The complete CREATE INDEX grammar for the supported MariaDB lines permits column key parts and documented index options but defines no WHERE predicate or partial-index clause.

observations.result: Both the non-unique and unique CREATE INDEX statements fail with a syntax error at their WHERE predicate.
Both statements fail with the MariaDB syntax error at WHERE; the unique case includes the compound Name predicate.
Both statements fail with the same syntax error at WHERE, confirming that MariaDB 11.8 has not added filtered-index grammar.

activeDispositions.providerWorkaroundAssessment: Ignoring the predicate would silently change index storage and, for unique indexes, constraint semantics. MySQL functional key parts and generated columns can emulate only predicates accepted by generated-expression restrictions; MariaDB requires a different generated-column shape. Both approaches add synthetic schema state, change the index column identity, and cannot preserve the general relational filter contract for arbitrary predicates. There is no general semantics-preserving provider rewrite across all supported targets.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when a supported MySQL or MariaDB release adds a native predicate clause for CREATE INDEX or another native index form that preserves arbitrary relational filter semantics and reverse-engineered index identity.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core rejects ExecuteDelete directly over a grouped projection whose shaper is an entity.

primarySources.title: Issue 28525: Bulk Delete on result of First family in projection
primarySources.supports: The open backlog issue contains the same official specification shape and states that EF Core's entity projection shaper and delete structure cannot currently represent it.

observations.result: All 12 sync and async invocations fail before provider SQL generation with ExecuteDeleteOnNonEntityType.
All 12 invocations fail at the same EF Core non-entity-projection boundary before provider SQL generation.
All 12 invocations fail at the same EF Core non-entity-projection boundary before provider SQL generation.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: RelationalQueryableMethodTranslatingExpressionVisitor.TranslateExecuteDelete rejects the shaped query before IsValidSelectExpressionForExecuteDelete or the provider SQL generator is invoked. A provider cannot recover the discarded entity projection through SQL translation hooks.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when dotnet/efcore issue 28525 closes or the consumed EF Core patch changes its grouped entity projection or ExecuteDelete translation.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot bind entity key properties from a GroupBy projection followed by First or FirstOrDefault.

primarySources.title: Issue 26753: Property binding on the result entity from grouping.First
primarySources.supports: The open backlog issue states that the shaped query produced by GroupBy followed by First is not an entity reference, so mapped property binding fails.

observations.result: All 14 sync and async invocations fail while EF Core binds EF.Property for the grouped First or FirstOrDefault entity, before provider SQL generation.
All 14 invocations fail at the same EF Core property-binding boundary before provider SQL generation.
All 14 invocations fail at the same EF Core property-binding boundary before provider SQL generation.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: RelationalSqlTranslatingExpressionVisitor fails to rewrite entity equality because the GroupBy/First shaper no longer exposes an entity reference. The provider receives neither a SqlExpression nor an update/delete tree, so a method translator or SQL generator cannot intervene.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when dotnet/efcore issue 26753 closes or the consumed EF Core patch changes grouped First entity property binding.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core rejects ExecuteUpdate on a non-leaf TPC entity before provider-owned update validation.

primarySources.title: Inheritance bulk-update specification skip
primarySources.supports: The official EF Core 10.0.8 specification marks Update_where_hierarchy_subquery skipped before provider subclasses run it.

primarySources.title: Relational ExecuteUpdate translation
primarySources.supports: TranslateExecuteUpdate rejects TpcTablesExpression before calling the provider-overridable IsValidSelectExpressionForExecuteUpdate method.

observations.result: Both TPC fixture variants fail in sync and async mode with ExecuteOperationOnTPC before provider update validation.
Both TPC fixture variants fail at the same EF Core TpcTablesExpression guard before provider update validation.
Both TPC fixture variants fail at the same EF Core TpcTablesExpression guard before provider update validation.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: The TPC base entity spans multiple concrete tables. EF Core deliberately rejects its TpcTablesExpression before the provider's native update-shape hook is called, so no provider extension point receives a translatable update tree.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when the consumed EF Core patch removes the TpcTablesExpression guard or documents multi-table ExecuteUpdate support for non-leaf TPC entities.

activeDispositions.summary: MariaDB cannot express a correlated derived table because FROM-subqueries cannot be correlated and the JOIN grammar has no LATERAL derived-table form.

primarySources.title: Subquery Limitations
primarySources.supports: The Correlated Subqueries section states that subqueries in the FROM clause cannot be correlated.

primarySources.title: JOIN Syntax
primarySources.supports: The complete table_reference and join_table grammar for MariaDB 11.4 through 11.8 has no LATERAL production.

observations.result: 160 affected invocations fail: 36 JSON queries and 124 Northwind query or include shapes. Representative failures are ERROR 1054 for an outer column below a derived-table boundary and the provider's explicit correlated-derived-table capability exception.
The same 160 invocations fail at the correlated FROM-subquery or missing LATERAL boundary as MariaDB 11.4.

activeDispositions.providerWorkaroundAssessment: The provider flattens APPLY into ordinary joins when cardinality, null extension, ordering, and pagination semantics can be preserved; JSON_TABLE also references preceding tables directly where the relational tree permits it. The remaining tests require per-outer-row composition after DISTINCT, grouping, ordering, filtering, pagination, set operations, or nested collection shaping. That composition introduces a correlated derived-table boundary which cannot be flattened without changing results. MariaDB provides neither correlation in FROM nor an equivalent LATERAL join operator, so the general relational operation cannot be emitted as server-side SQL. Client evaluation would change the specification contract and is not accepted as a provider workaround.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when MariaDB documents either correlated FROM-subqueries or a LATERAL/APPLY join production for every supported MariaDB target.

activeDispositions.summary: MariaDB JSON_TABLE cannot extract a JSON object or array into a JSON-typed result column.

primarySources.title: JSON_TABLE
primarySources.supports: The Extracting a Subdocument into a Column section states that JSON_TABLE does not allow extraction of a JSON subdocument into a JSON column.

observations.result: Both methods fail for sync and async data rows because the required owned JSON subdocument is returned as NULL; the materializer reports Nullable object must have a value.
Both methods fail for sync and async data rows with the same NULL subdocument materialization failure as MariaDB 11.4.

activeDispositions.providerWorkaroundAssessment: The projection requires the complete owned JSON subdocument as a value so EF Core can materialize the owned graph. Extracting individual scalar members would not preserve arbitrary nested content or the specification's JSON materialization semantics. MariaDB's documented JSON_TABLE result-column restriction therefore removes the required server-side rowset operation.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when MariaDB documents JSON_TABLE support for extracting a JSON subdocument into a JSON result column on every supported MariaDB target.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot identify a stable collection identifier for a JSON collection property projection followed by Distinct.

primarySources.title: Query/Json: projecting individual properties of JSON collection with Distinct fails due to insufficient information
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core backlog issue contains this exact specification query and explains that EF Core lacks sufficient identifier information for the projected JSON collection.

observations.result: Both async modes fail in EF Core collection-shaping translation before provider SQL execution.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core collection-shaping boundary as MySQL 8.4.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core collection-shaping boundary as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: The failure is raised while EF Core assigns identifiers to the shaped JSON collection. No database-specific SQL operation can add the missing framework projection metadata.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: The probe passes after dotnet/efcore issue 31397 is fixed in the consumed EF Core line.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot translate GroupBy followed by ordering on a JSON scalar and FirstOrDefault.

primarySources.title: JSON/Query: translate groupby followed by orderby json scalar + FirstOrDefault
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core backlog issue contains the exact GroupBy, JSON scalar OrderBy, and FirstOrDefault shape.

observations.result: Both async modes fail in RelationalSqlTranslatingExpressionVisitor while binding the owned JSON property.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core property-binding boundary as MySQL 8.4.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core property-binding boundary as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: The framework rejects the expression before a provider SQL tree exists. The provider cannot compensate with engine-specific SQL generation.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: The probe passes after dotnet/efcore issue 29287 is fixed in the consumed EF Core line.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot bind a JSON owned property above a FirstOrDefault subquery for structural comparison.

primarySources.title: Json/Query: support subquery FirstOrDefault scenario with binding to property on top of that
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core backlog issue contains the exact JSON FirstOrDefault property-binding and comparison query.

observations.result: Both async modes fail inside EF Core with an invalid cast from JsonQueryExpression to StructuralTypeProjectionExpression.
Both async modes fail with the same EF Core internal expression-type cast as MySQL 8.4.
Both async modes fail with the same EF Core internal expression-type cast as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: The invalid cast occurs in EF Core structural equality rewriting before provider SQL generation. A database-provider SQL rewrite cannot intercept that framework-internal type mismatch.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: The probe passes after dotnet/efcore issue 28733 is fixed in the consumed EF Core line.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot backtrack from a nested JSON owned entity to its parent during query translation.

primarySources.title: Json/Query: allow backtracking into parent json entities
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core issue tracks parent backtracking for JSON-owned entities and is the issue referenced by the upstream skipped specification test.

observations.result: Both async modes fail during EF Core owned-navigation expansion before provider SQL execution.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core navigation-expansion boundary as MySQL 8.4.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core navigation-expansion boundary as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: Parent backtracking is absent from EF Core's JSON navigation model. The provider receives no translatable expression on which an engine-specific implementation could operate.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: The probe passes after dotnet/efcore issue 28645 is fixed in the consumed EF Core line.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot preserve a nested JSON collection projection through two subquery pushdowns.

primarySources.title: Select + Distinct + Select Collection results in incorrect SQL and results
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core issue tracks collection projection loss through composed select and pushdown shapes and is referenced by the upstream specification test.

observations.result: Both async modes fail in RelationalProjectionBindingExpressionVisitor because the nested owned JSON collection cannot be translated after the second pushdown.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core projection-binding boundary as MySQL 8.4.
Both async modes fail at the same EF Core projection-binding boundary as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: The adjacent single-pushdown test is explicitly enabled and passes on Doka. Only the second framework pushdown loses the nested collection expression before provider SQL generation.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: The double-pushdown probe passes after dotnet/efcore issue 24263 is fixed in the consumed EF Core line.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core null comparison semantics are incorrect for a property converter that handles nulls.

primarySources.title: Query: property with converter which handles nulls, can/will give wrong results when compared to null
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core issue tracks wrong null-comparison results for converters that handle nulls and is referenced by the upstream specification test.

observations.result: Both async modes return two rows instead of the one row required by converter-aware null semantics.
Both async modes reproduce the same two-versus-one framework null-semantics mismatch as MySQL 8.4.
Both async modes reproduce the same two-versus-one framework null-semantics mismatch as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: EF Core performs null-semantics rewriting around value conversion before provider-specific SQL generation. The identical upstream skipped test and issue isolate this as framework behavior rather than an engine capability.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: The probe passes after dotnet/efcore issue 29416 is fixed in the consumed EF Core line.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core cannot expand a navigation reached through a grouping key after the grouping operation.

primarySources.title: Expand navigations on grouping key
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core issue explains that grouping-key navigations cannot be expanded through the normal translation path and tracks a framework-level correlated-subquery implementation.

observations.result: Both sync and async invocations return a null nested navigation component where the specification expects customer VINET.
Both sync and async invocations reproduce the same null nested navigation component as MySQL 8.4.
Both sync and async invocations reproduce the same null nested navigation component as MySQL 8.4.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: Navigation expansion and grouping projection construction are owned by EF Core. The navigation is absent from the translated projection before the provider receives a recoverable relational shape, so provider SQL generation cannot reconstruct the missing navigation path.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when dotnet/efcore issue 29014 closes or when the consumed EF Core patch changes grouping-key navigation expansion.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core can bind an aggregate from an outer grouping to an inner grouping when equivalent aggregate expressions are simplified.

primarySources.title: Simplification of Count(*) with multiple group by can generate wrong result
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core issue demonstrates that aggregate simplification can rebind an outer grouping count to the inner grouping and produce incorrect results.

observations.result: Both methods reproduce the framework aggregate-binding defect in sync and async mode; the projected count is 4 where the specification requires 8.
The third projection returns 4 instead of 8 in both modes. The other projection reaches MariaDB's correlated-derived-table boundary after EF Core has produced the same incorrect aggregate structure.
The third projection returns 4 instead of 8 in both modes. The other projection reaches the same correlated-derived-table boundary as MariaDB 11.4 after framework translation.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: EF Core performs aggregate simplification and grouping-scope binding before provider-specific SQL generation. The resulting relational tree no longer identifies the aggregate as belonging to the outer grouping, so the provider cannot infer and restore the original LINQ scope.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when dotnet/efcore issue 27130 closes or when the consumed EF Core patch changes aggregate simplification across nested groupings.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core does not preserve every component of nested anonymous-object join keys during relational translation.

primarySources.title: Query: invalid SQL generated when doing join with nested anonymous key selectors
primarySources.supports: The open EF Core issue reproduces a nested anonymous join key whose relational predicate ends after AND because a nested key component is lost.

observations.result: The Join method emits a predicate ending in AND before ORDER BY. The GroupJoin method reaches EF Core's expected translation-failure assertion; both sync and async modes reproduce the upstream boundary.
Both methods reproduce the same incomplete-predicate or framework translation-failure behavior as MySQL 8.4 in sync and async mode.
Both methods reproduce the same incomplete-predicate or framework translation-failure behavior as MySQL 8.4 in sync and async mode.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: EF Core decomposes structural join keys before provider SQL generation. It either emits an incomplete relational predicate or returns NotTranslated after nested members have been discarded, so a provider SQL generator cannot recover the original anonymous-object components.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when dotnet/efcore issue 35028 closes or when the consumed EF Core patch changes structural join-key translation.

activeDispositions.summary: Doka first ships on EF Core 10 and cannot possess provider-generated EF Core 2.1, 2.2, or 3.0 snapshots from an earlier public release.
activeDispositions.rationale: Fabricating historical provider snapshots now would only test symmetry with newly invented fixtures. The upstream compatibility premise is structurally absent rather than unsupported by either database engine.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Never for these pre-release versions. Add real compatibility snapshots only after Doka has published a version whose snapshots must remain readable by a later release.

activeDispositions.summary: EF Core rejects shadow properties on complex types during model validation before provider SQL generation.

primarySources.title: ModelBuilderTest.ComplexType.cs at v10.0.8
primarySources.supports: The official complex-type contract marks the affected facts with ConditionalFact(Skip = "Issue #35613").

primarySources.title: ModelBuilderTest.ComplexCollections.cs at v10.0.8
primarySources.supports: The official complex-collection contract marks the affected facts with issue-linked ConditionalFact skips.

primarySources.title: ModelValidator.cs at v10.0.8
primarySources.supports: ValidatePropertyMapping throws ComplexTypeShadowProperty when it finds a non-discriminator shadow property on a complex type and identifies issue 35613 in the enforcement source.

observations.result: The in-memory model-building probe reports 130 failures, 1366 passes, and 12 inherited upstream skips; every reactivated failure terminates in EF Core ModelValidator with ComplexTypeShadowProperty before provider SQL generation.
The target-independent model-building probe produces the same 130 framework failures, 1366 passes, and 12 inherited upstream skips.
The target-independent model-building probe produces the same 130 framework failures, 1366 passes, and 12 inherited upstream skips.

activeDispositions.frameworkBoundaryAssessment: MySqlModelValidator delegates to EF Core RelationalModelValidator, which reaches the core ModelValidator rejection before any relational command tree or provider SQL can exist. Bypassing that validation in the provider would create metadata semantics that EF Core itself does not support.
activeDispositions.reevaluateWhen: Re-run the probe when issue 35613 closes, when the consumed EF Core patch removes any linked upstream skip, or when ModelValidator no longer rejects shadow properties on complex types.

providerWorkarounds.engineRestriction: Both database families reject LIMIT directly inside an IN, ALL, ANY, or SOME subquery.
providerWorkarounds.implementation: MySqlQuerySqlGenerator.GenerateIn preserves the LINQ behavior by placing the limited single-column query behind a derived-table boundary.

primarySources.title: Restrictions on Subqueries
primarySources.supports: The manual documents ERROR 1235 for LIMIT within IN, ALL, ANY, or SOME subqueries.

primarySources.title: Subquery Limitations
primarySources.supports: The manual documents ERROR 1235 for the same LIMIT and IN, ALL, ANY, or SOME combination.

providerWorkarounds.verification: Verified 2026-07-27 against EF Core 10.0.8 and 10.0.10 in the full functional suite with both specification methods active. For each EF Core version, MySQL 8.4 passed 1234, failed 0, skipped 10; MariaDB 11.4 and 11.8 each passed 1192, failed 0, skipped 31.

providerWorkarounds.engineRestriction: MySQL 8.4 may return the wrong result for EXISTS over JSON_TABLE because of optimizer bug 114897.
providerWorkarounds.implementation: MySqlQuerySqlGenerator.GenerateExists emits a limited scalar subquery for the affected MySQL JSON_TABLE shape, avoiding the faulty semijoin transformation while preserving EXISTS and NOT EXISTS semantics.

primarySources.title: Bug #114897: json_table and exists make a bug
primarySources.supports: The verified bug report reproduces an incorrect result for WHERE EXISTS over JSON_TABLE.

providerWorkarounds.verification: Verified 2026-07-27 against EF Core 10.0.8 and 10.0.10. The sync and async specification invocations pass on MySQL 8.4 after the rewrite, and each complete MySQL suite passed 1234, failed 0, skipped 10.

providerWorkarounds.engineRestriction: Both database families cap the relevant schema identifiers at 64 characters.
providerWorkarounds.implementation: MySqlConventionSetBuilder registers RelationalMaxIdentifierLengthConvention with a limit of 64 so EF Core truncates names deterministically and adds collision suffixes before DDL generation.
